title: fix(app-shell): the dashboard designer's selected-widget strip resolves a per-locale widget title (objectui#10847)
body:
Fixes #10847

Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

`DashboardWidget.title` is the spec's `I18nLabel`: a string or an inline per-locale map. In the dashboard designer, `SelectedWidgetStrip` in `DashboardPreview.tsx` read it as `(widget.title as string | undefined) ?? widget.id ?? ''` and rendered that as a React child. Selecting a widget whose title is `{ 'en-US': 'Revenue', 'zh-CN': '收入' }` threw "Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {en-US, zh-CN})". The error boundary then replaced the whole preview with "Preview failed to render". The rename draft was seeded from the same value, and the save wrote one plain string over the stored title.

## What changed

- **Display and seed.** The strip resolves the title with `resolveInlineI18nLabel(widget.title, locale)`, which is the spec's `resolveI18nLabel`. It passes the same designer `locale` prop that `handleWidgetClick` already uses for the selection label. The rename draft is seeded from that resolved string. No second resolver was added.
- **Save.** `handleRenameWidget` now writes `setLocalized(w.title, locale, trimmed)` from `@object-ui/i18n` and no longer writes `trimmed` directly. For a map title, only the designer locale's entry is replaced or added, and every other locale is kept. A string title, or a missing one, still gets a plain string, as before. `DashboardWidgetInspector` already uses this read/write pair for its title input, so the strip and the inspector write an edit to the same entry. The inspector's title field edits the same entry through the same read/write pair, `resolveInlineI18nLabel` and `setLocalized`; editing every locale from one surface is still an open question.
- The `SelectedWidgetStrip` docblock and a comment on `handleRenameWidget` now describe this.

### How the ruling's `{ ...map, [locale]: draft }` is met

`setLocalized` returns `{ ...map, [KEY]: draft }`. KEY is the entry the resolver shows for that locale: the exact tag, then the base language, then a region sibling. If none of those exists, KEY is the designer locale itself. In the card's case (`{ en-US, zh-CN }` edited in `zh-CN`), the result is exactly `{ ...map, 'zh-CN': draft }`. A literal `[locale]` write gives a different result only when the map stores the locale under another spelling, such as an `en` key while the designer locale is `en-US`. There, a literal write would add a new `en-US` entry and leave the `en` string the author saw unchanged. `setLocalized` edits the entry the author was looking at. The map is never flattened in either case.

## Mechanism assumptions, measured

- **S1 holds.** The crash reproduces on base `4aebea0` through the real `DashboardPreview` and the real `DashboardRenderer`. See the red run below; the error text is as quoted above.
- **S2, which locale.** The preview's own resolver (`handleWidgetClick`, which builds the selection label) uses the designer `locale` prop. That prop comes from `useMetadataLocale()`, which collapses the UI language to `zh-CN` or `en-US`. The grid cards inside `DashboardRenderer` resolve widget titles with `pickLocalized(title, language)` against the raw UI language from `useObjectTranslation()`. The strip follows the ruling and the preview's own call, so it uses the designer locale. The two agree for en and zh UI languages with conventional keys. Acceptance notes describe where they can differ.

## Tests

New file `DashboardPreview.i18nTitle-10847.test.tsx`. It runs through the real `DashboardPreview` and `DashboardRenderer`. A host component keeps the draft and the selection in state, and each test selects the widget by clicking its cell on the canvas.

1. Map title, designer locale `zh-CN`: the widget selects without reaching the error boundary, and the strip shows `收入`.
2. Rename `收入` to `营收`: the draft is seeded with `收入`, the stored title is `{ 'en-US': 'Revenue', 'zh-CN': '营收' }`, the selection label is `营收`, and the strip re-renders `营收`.
3. A map without the designer locale (`{ 'en-US': 'Revenue' }` edited in `zh-CN`): the strip shows the fallback `Revenue`, and the rename adds `zh-CN` while keeping `en-US`.
4. Control: a plain-string title shows as written, and a rename stores a plain string.

- **Red on base** (fix absent, new test present): `Tests  3 failed | 1 passed (4)`. The three map tests fail with "Objects are not valid as a React child". The string control passes.
- **Green with the fix:** `Test Files  2 passed (2)`, `Tests  9 passed (9)` for the new file plus `DashboardPreview.loneWidget.test.tsx`.
- **Ablation.** The fix was committed first (`a97096e`). The mutation went through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the `setLocalized` write was replaced by the flattening `title: trimmed,`. The anchor count went from 1 to 0 and the blob from `a3187e12ce62` to `daeb70801893`. Result: `Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)`. Tests 2 and 3 went red with `Received: "营收"` and `Received: "收入"`, a flat string where the map was expected. Tests 1 and 4 stayed green. The file was restored with `git checkout HEAD -- ABS_PATH`. Afterwards the blob matched HEAD (`a3187e12ce62`) and `git diff HEAD` was empty. The test imports `./DashboardPreview` by relative path, which is source, so neither leg needed a build.

## Gates, run at `c527690` and carried to `753c2b0`

The delta from `c527690` to `753c2b0` is prose only (the changeset text and one docblock), so these results carry forward. CI re-ran the gates green at `753c2b0` (43 check runs: 40 success, 3 skipped, 0 failure).

- **Build.** `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2` built the dependency closure first: `Tasks: 28 successful, 28 total`.
- **Type-check.** `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` ran `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` and exited 0. The new test file is in `tsconfig.test.json`'s file list (`--listFilesOnly` finds it once).
- **Tests, first ring:** the 9 test files that name `DashboardPreview` (found by `git grep`) plus `DashboardWidgetInspector.test.tsx`. Result: `Test Files  9 passed (9)`, `Tests  76 passed (76)`.
- **Tests, second ring:** the 11 test files that reach the preview registry (`previews/index`, `getMetadataPreview`, `resolveMetadataPreview`) plus `DashboardDefaultInspector.test.tsx`. Result: `Test Files  12 passed (12)`, `Tests  60 passed (60)`.
- **ESLint, narrowed to the 2 changed files** (`--no-inline-config --format json`): 2 files, 0 errors, 8 warnings. The base version of `DashboardPreview.tsx` has the same 8 warnings under the same rules, so none are new. Type-aware linting is not enabled: the printed config has neither `parserOptions.project` nor `projectService`. No custom rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the file system. So this diff cannot change the lint result of any file it does not touch.
- **Changesets:** `check-changeset-presence` reports "2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)". `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-overwrite` and `check-changeset-claims` all exit 0.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only -> exit 0`.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape` and `check:phantom-deps` all report OK and exit 0.

**NOT MEASURED**

- **The full `@object-ui/app-shell` suite** (837 test files). A 182-file run over `metadata-admin/` and the matching `studio-design/` tests hit the 540s timeout on the shared container (exit 124, no result). I narrowed it to the two rings above. CI runs the full suite.
- **`check:eager-closure`.** It reads the console's production build output, which was not built locally. The only new import is `setLocalized` from `@object-ui/i18n`, and app-shell already imports that function in `DashboardWidgetInspector` and `ReportDefaultInspector`.
- **Repo-wide `pnpm lint`.** Left to CI.

## Changeset

`.changeset/10847-dashboard-strip-i18n-title.md`, a `patch` for `@object-ui/app-shell`.

## Acceptance notes

- **The strip and the grid cards can resolve with different locales.** The strip, the selection label and the inspector all resolve with the designer locale (`en-US` or `zh-CN`). The grid cards resolve with the raw UI language. Suppose the UI language is neither English nor Chinese, for example `ja`, and the map has a `ja` entry. Then the card shows the `ja` string, while the strip, the selection label and the inspector show the `en-US` entry, and a rename edits `en-US`. This split between the designer chrome and the runtime cards existed before this PR; this PR only brings the strip in line with the chrome. It is an observation, not filed. Carrier: none (承接者:无).
- **New widgets get an English title.** `handleAddWidget` still seeds a new widget's title as a plain English string (`New` plus the type label) in every designer locale. That is authored data, not chrome. It is outside this card and not filed. Carrier: none (承接者:无).
- The other designer surfaces that still show English (`PreviewShell`, `ScreenPreview`, `flow-sim-validate`) belong to objectui#10848 and are not touched here.
